## Summary
Audit events already go through a dedicated `AUDIT` logger with ids only. What is missing is a separate appender and a retained sink; keep the ids-only rule intact.

## Findings
| id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARC-001 | info | observability | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/audit/AuditLogger.java:19 | `LoggerFactory.getLogger("AUDIT")`: audit events already use a dedicated AUDIT logger | Keep the logger name as the routing key. |
| ARC-002 | medium | observability | sample-app/src/main/resources/application.yml:41 | Only `logging.level.AUDIT: INFO`; no logback appender separates audit events from application logs | Add `logback-spring.xml` with a JSON appender for `AUDIT` (`additivity=false`) and a marker field `stream=audit`. |
| ARC-003 | medium | security | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/audit/AuditLogger.java:21 | Events carry action, resource id and staff username (ids only) | Keep ids-only; add a test asserting no PHI fields. The six-year store still holds usernames, so restrict access to it. |
| ARC-004 | low | deployability | sample-app/k8s/deployment.yaml:25 | The container logs to stdout | Route the `stream=audit` lines to the retained store with the cluster log collector; choose the store in an ADR. |

## Decisions
- Separation happens in the log pipeline, not in application code: no new runtime dependency.
